newsitem.title: UK: Pearson faces producers' revolt - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pearson faces producers' revolt - paper.

text.p: Media company Pearson is facing the threat of a revolt among its leading television producers and writers if it fails to retain Greg Dyke, chief executive of the group's TV subsidiary, the Observer newspaper said.
Pearson TV is the country's largest independent programme producer.

Dyke is known to want to lead a leveraged buyout of Pearson TV from the parent company and if he fails he is likely to leave, putting a number of Pearson TV's production contracts under threat, the paper said.
Pearson shares closed Friday 2p lower at 766.33p.

On Friday Pearson said that it had sold its entire 10 percent stake in Hong Kong's Television Broadcasts Ltd for 111.1 million stg. Analysts said this appeared to remove a plank in Dyke's television strategy. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
